nodes.description: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) places a single spermatozoon directly into the oocyte, so fertilisation no longer depends on hyperactivated motility or zona pellucida penetration. Men with type I globozoospermia who wish to conceive must use ICSI, but fertilisation rates with ICSI in globozoospermia are much lower than in other male infertility, and assisted oocyte activation (AOA) is reported to restore them. No ICSI outcome has been reported for a CATSPERT patient.

nodes.description: CatSper tau is a CatSper channel subunit with a calcium-dependent C2 membrane-binding domain. It reaches the flagellum on its own and acts as the main component that targets the channel complex to the flagellar membrane. It is not needed to assemble a working channel. In mice, truncating the C2 domain was enough to stop the channel being carried into the nanodomains of developing spermatids. The human variant p.His113Arg lies in the same C2 domain, but its effect on the protein has not been tested.
